title: The first click gets a 404
description: Your shortener handles 400 creates/s and 40,000 redirects/s at peak. Redirects use Redis, then read replicas on a miss. New links sometimes return 404 on their first click, then work a second later. Existing links are fast. How would you fix the first-click problem without sending every redirect to the primary?

options.text: Cache a newly committed link at creation, and use a primary fallback for replica misses that might be lag.
options.explanation: The unique insert still decides creation. Caching the committed row helps the first click, while a targeted primary fallback handles replica lag without moving all reads to the primary.

options.text: Shard the link table by alias and keep the same replica-only miss path.
options.explanation: More shards may add capacity later, but their replicas can still lag. The first-click freshness problem remains.

options.text: Keep negative cache entries longer so repeated 404s do not reach the replicas.
options.explanation: Negative caching protects the database from unknown aliases, but a long-lived false 404 would hide a newly created link for longer.

options.text: Return a 301 for successful redirects so browsers avoid future lookups.
options.explanation: A redirect status cannot fix a lookup that returns 404. Permanent caching also conflicts with revocable links.
